nights_sources.quote: We recommend spending at least 3 days in Bangkok, though 4 or 5 days is better if you can manage it.

In two weeks in Thailand, you should be able to visit: Bangkok (3 nights), Chiang Mai (3 nights), Chiang Rai (0-1 nights), Koh Tao/Koh Phangan/Koh Samui (3 nights), Khao Sok (2 nights), and Phuket/Krabi (3 nights).
Three days give you enough time to visit the Grand Palace complex, the main temples, a rooftop bar, and the best of Chinatown and Talat Noi.

do.what: Grand Palace + Temple of the Emerald Buddha (Wat Phra Kaew) - go at opening, book online

source.quote: The highlight is the Temple of the Emerald Buddha, which sits at the heart of the complex.

do.what: Wat Pho - the 46 m gilded Reclining Buddha (plus Thai massage at the temple school)

source.quote: It is most famous for the Reclining Buddha: a 46-metre gilded figure that fills an entire building.

do.what: Wat Arun (Temple of Dawn) across the river - via Chao Phraya Express Boat

source.quote: Wat Arun is on the western bank of the river, and it’s one of Bangkok’s most photogenic landmarks.

do.what: Chinatown / Yaowarat Road street-food dinner (stalls from ~6 pm)

source.quote: Yaowarat Road, the main artery, is a riot of gold shops, seafood restaurants, herbal medicine vendors, and neon signs.

do.what: Sky Bar at Lebua - the Hangover II rooftop bar over the river (Silom)

source.quote: Sky Bar at Lebua — Bangkok’s most famous rooftop bar, partly due to its appearance in The Hangover Part II.

do.what: Chatuchak Weekend Market (Sat-Sun only)

source.quote: Chatuchak itself is one of the largest markets in the world.

do.what: Khao San Road night out

source.quote: But Khao San Road is also genuinely entertaining, and it is hard not to get swept up in it.

do.what: Day trip: Maeklong Railway Market (market on an active train track) + Damnoen Saduak Floating Market

source.quote: On the second day in Thailand, we suggest taking the classical Maeklong Railway Market and Damnoen Saduak Floating Market day trip from Bangkok.

sleep.area: Sukhumvit (shopping, nightlife, BTS/MRT) or Rattanakosin/Banglamphu near Khao San Road (temples, old city)

source.quote: The best area to stay depends on what you want to do. For temples and markets, the Rattanakosin/Banglamphu area (near Khao San Road) is convenient. For shopping, nightlife, and easy transport, Sukhumvit is the best base.

next.how: Domestic flight Bangkok (BKK/DMK) -> Krabi International Airport (KBV), ~1h20 (Thai AirAsia, Thai Airways, Bangkok Airways, Thai Vietjet listed); then ~30-40 min road transfer or airport bus (~1 h) to Ao Nang.

source.quote: Traveling by plane is the fastest way to get from Bangkok to Krabi.

more_sources.quote: Fastest Transport 1h 20m
Krabi International Airport is about 40 minutes away by car.
There is an air-conditioned bus service from the airport to Ao Nang and Nopparat Thara Beach (just after Ao Nang).

photo_queries: Wat Arun sunset Chao Phraya river

research.place_en: Krabi - Ao Nang (with day trips to Railay)

nights_sources.quote: Three days is the sweet spot.
We suggest staying between three and seven days in Krabi.

do.what: Railay Beach (Hebrew: ריילי) - car-free peninsula, longtail from Ao Nang; Railay West beach

source.quote: Start at Railay Beach , easily one of the most photogenic stretches of coast in Thailand.

do.what: Phra Nang Cave Beach (next to Railay) - karst tower rising out of the sand, the postcard shot

source.quote: Phra Nang is the postcard shot. Don’t skip it.

do.what: Railay viewpoint & hidden lagoon hike (steep, hand ropes)

source.quote: The climb to the top takes about 20-25 minutes and to the viewpoint another 10 minutes.

do.what: 4 Islands longtail tour from Ao Nang beach (Poda Island, Chicken Island, Tup, Phra Nang) ~900-1,200 THB

source.quote: The main beach at Ao Nang is the departure point for boats to a number of places, including the nearby resort of Rai Leh, which cannot be accessed by road, Poda Island and Chicken Island.

do.what: Hong Island tour - enclosed lagoon ringed by karst walls

source.quote: Afternoon on the water again, but this time Hong Island — a smaller, quieter archipelago than Phi Phi with a stunning enclosed lagoon ringed by karst walls.

do.what: Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) - 1,237 steps to a 360-degree summit view, go at 7:30

source.quote: The climb is 1,237 steps to the summit, and the Thai sun has zero mercy.

do.what: Emerald Pool + Klong Thom hot springs (go at opening)

source.quote: It’s a jungle spring the color of green sea glass, and just a few minutes away sit the Klong Thom hot springs — natural warm-water pools cascading between rocks.

do.what: Sunset on Ao Nang beach behind the karst islands

source.quote: The sky lighting up orange behind the karst islands offshore is worth planting yourself at a beachfront table for a full hour.

sleep.area: Ao Nang (beach strip, walking distance to the boats; Railay is pricier - optional 1 night there)

source.quote: Ao Nang is the base we recommend — it’s walking distance to the pier where nearly every boat tour leaves from, dinner options are everywhere, and it’s cheaper than Railay by a wide margin.

more_sources.quote: Ao Nang is filled with accommodation options , but if you want to get away from the crowds, consider spending a night on the isolated Railay Beach.

next.how: Ferry (or speedboat) from Ao Nang's Nopparat Thara pier to Tonsai Pier, Phi Phi Don, ~1.5-2 h by ferry; hotel pickup usually included. Operators listed include Andaman Wave Master; ~21 van-transfer+boat departures a day on 12Go.

source.quote: From Ao Nang: 400 baht one way (including transfer from hotel to Noppharat Peir) 0930 and 1530.

more_sources.quote: The travel time from Ao Nang to Koh Phi Phi can vary depending on the mode of transportation you choose. All things considered, the whole journey should take from 1 to 4 hours.
Sailing time from Phuket or Krabi is 1.5-2 hours.

photo_queries: Railay Beach longtail boat limestone cliffs
Phra Nang Cave Beach Krabi aerial

nights_sources.quote: If you’re short on time, a well-planned Koh Phi Phi 2-day itinerary is more than enough to enjoy the island’s highlights.
Day trip or 1 to 2 nights on Phi Phi Don

do.what: Phi Phi Viewpoint hike (186 m) - sunrise/sunset view of the twin bays

source.quote: Walk up to the viewpoint, 186 m above sea level (a very steep walk of between 10–25 min, depending on your fitness), to get a breathtaking view of the entire island, particularly at dawn or sunset (bring a torch).

do.what: Maya Bay on Phi Phi Leh ('The Beach' film) - boardwalk from Loh Samah, no swimming, closed Aug-Sep

source.quote: Maya Bay reopened on 1 January 2022 with strict new rules.

do.what: Pi Leh Lagoon - cliff-ringed inlet on Phi Phi Leh (boat tour stop)

source.quote: Pi Ley is a large inlet on Koh Phi Phi Ley in-between Phaya Naak Cave and Loh Samah. The whole inlet is surrounded by vertical cliffs.

do.what: Longtail/speedboat island tour: Maya Bay, Viking Cave, Loh Dalum, Monkey Beach, Bamboo Island

source.quote: Here are the usual places where boats will take you : Maya Bay (when open, which is not always predictable), Viking Cave (Used to be open to the public, but it’s now restricted), Loh Dalum Bay, Monkey Beach, Bamboo Island , and sometimes Mosquito Island next to it.

do.what: Bamboo Island - white sand, clear water, snorkelling

source.quote: Bamboo Island is a small, uninhabited island about 8 km northeast of the main Phi Phi island. It has white sand beaches, clear water and good snorkelling.

do.what: Loh Dalum Bay by day: kayak (from ~200 THB), the postcard turquoise bay

source.quote: Rent a kayak from Loh Dalum Beach (starting from 200 baht) and paddle around the island’s calm, clear waters.

do.what: Loh Dalum beach bars at night - fire shows, buckets, bean bags

source.quote: At night, head to the beach bars around Loh Dalum Beach. The atmosphere turns lively with fire shows, cocktails, and music under the stars.

do.what: Long Beach - walkable from Tonsai, snorkelling at Shark Point (blacktip reef sharks)

source.quote: Spend a few hours relaxing or snorkeling at Shark Point near Long Beach. If you’re lucky, you might spot harmless blacktip reef sharks.

sleep.area: Tonsai Village / Loh Dalum (between the two bays; convenient but loud) - quieter: Long Beach

source.quote: Ao Ton Sai is where most of the action is, be it restaurants, bars, hotels, or guesthouses. Most tourists stay at Ton Sai Bay because of the convenience.

more_sources.quote: I stayed at PP Princess Resort, and the location is what makes it special. The hotel sits right between Loh Dalum Bay and Tonsai town, so you get both.

next.how: Full travel day across to the Gulf: joint ticket from Tonsai Pier (departures ~08:45-10:30) = ferry to Krabi + van/bus to Don Sak/Surat Thani + ferry (e.g. Lomprayah) to Thong Sala; 7-16 h total. Faster alternative: ferry to Krabi or Phuket and fly Bangkok Airways to Koh Samui (daily Phuket-Samui flights), then 20-30 min ferry to Phangan.

source.quote: The travel time from Koh Phi Phi to Koh Phangan can vary depending on the mode of transportation you choose. All things considered, the whole journey should take from 7 to 16 hours.

more_sources.quote: From Koh Phi Phi to Koh Phangan starting from 08:45 Ton Sai Pier Koh Phi Phi until 10:30 Ton Sai Pier Koh Phi Phi
Koh Phi Phi to Koh Phangan, Ferry Express, Lomprayah
There are also daily flights to/from Phuket

photo_queries: Phi Phi viewpoint twin bays aerial
Maya Bay Phi Phi Leh turquoise

nights_sources.quote: Three days for the beaches and a snorkelling trip.

Once you’ve made your choice, we recommend spending at least 3 nights there, so you can properly enjoy the breathtaking beaches, snorkeling, diving, boat trips, fantastic food, and everything in between that these islands offer.

do.what: Full Moon Party at Haad Rin Sunrise Beach (one night a month - plan dates; also Half Moon Party)

source.quote: If you're after party heaven you can't do better than Haad Rin, an expanded village of beach bars, cheap chicken burgers, and low cut figure-hugging outfits. It is most popular one night a month, the night of the Full Moon Party.

do.what: Haad Rin - party beach (Haad Rin Nok, sunrise) vs. quieter Haad Rin Nai (sunset)

source.quote: Two sides: Haad Rin Nok (the party beach, east-facing, sunrise) and Haad Rin Nai (west-facing, quieter, sunset).

do.what: Bottle Beach (Haad Khuat) - by longtail from Chaloklum or hiking trail

source.quote: Best beach: Bottle Beach: reached by boat, hiking trail, or a rough road transfer

do.what: Thong Nai Pan Yai/Noi - sheltered bay, calm water

source.quote: Best for swimming: Thong Nai Pan Yai : sheltered bay, calm water, good restaurants

do.what: Than Sadet National Park waterfall hike

source.quote: For the nature-loving, head to Than Sadet National Park to hike up a waterfall.

do.what: Zen Beach sunset (west coast, Srithanu area)

source.quote: Best sunset: Zen Beach : rocky headland on the west coast, meditation-friendly atmosphere

do.what: Koh Ma - walk across the sandbar at low tide, snorkel with turtles/clownfish

source.quote: Koh Ma : a small island connected to the northwest tip by a sandbar. Shallow reef snorkelling (you can wade across at low tide).

do.what: Thong Sala markets: Phantip food market + Saturday Walking Street

source.quote: Saturday Walking Street (Thong Sala): weekly market with crafts, clothing, live music, and food stalls

sleep.area: Haad Rin (party / Full Moon) or Srithanu & Thong Nai Pan (quiet, beaches); Thong Sala = ferry pier, budget

source.quote: Haad Rin: Full Moon Party proximity. Quiet the rest of the month

more_sources.quote: Thong Nai Pan: best beaches, slightly isolated, romantic
Srithanu: wellness crowd, yoga studios, vegan restaurants

next.how: Ferry/speedboat Thong Sala -> Samui (Lomprayah, Seatran Discovery, Songserm, Haad Rin Queen from Haad Rin to Big Buddha pier); 20-30 min fastest, up to ~1 h on slower boats; ~92 departures a day listed.

source.quote: The west coast faces Koh Samui across a narrow strait; ferries make the hop in as little as 30 minutes, and our 5-day Koh Samui and Koh Phangan itinerary covers both islands in one trip.

more_sources.quote: Fastest Transport 20m
Koh Phangan to Koh Samui, Ferry High Speed Ferry, Seatran Discovery
Koh Phangan to Koh Samui, Ferry Express, Lomprayah

photo_queries: Koh Ma sandbar Koh Phangan drone

nights_sources.quote: 3 days in Koh Samui is enough time to experience the highlights.
Three days covers the main beaches, Big Buddha, and a day trip.

do.what: Big Buddha (Wat Phra Yai) - 12 m golden Buddha, sunset spot

source.quote: Big Buddha Temple (Wat Phra Yai) is a well-known free landmark and is impossible to miss with its 12 meter tall golden statue.

do.what: Wat Plai Laem - lakeside temple with the 18-armed Guanyin, next to Big Buddha

source.quote: A colourful lakeside temple complex with an 18-armed Guanyin statue rising from the water. It is close to Big Buddha, making the two temples easy to combine.

do.what: Fisherman's Village, Bophut - Friday Walking Street night market

source.quote: The Friday Walking Street is the island’s best market: live music, seafood grills, handmade goods, and a genuinely good atmosphere.

do.what: Ang Thong National Marine Park day tour - 42 islands, kayaking, snorkelling, Emerald Lake viewpoint (closed ~1 Nov-15 Dec)

source.quote: Mu Ko Ang Thong contains 42 islands, with tours commonly combining kayaking, snorkelling, and the Emerald Lake viewpoint on Koh Mae Koh.

do.what: Chaweng Beach + Chaweng Night Market

source.quote: Chaweng Beach is one of the most popular beaches with a vibrant atmosphere and a host of beach clubs offering delicious cocktails.

do.what: Lamai Beach + Hin Ta Hin Yai (Grandfather & Grandmother Rocks)

source.quote: One must-see spot near Lamai Beach is the Hin Ta & Hin Ya Rocks , also known as the Grandfather & Grandmother Rocks.

do.what: Na Mueang (Na Muang) Waterfall 1 & 2

source.quote: A walk of about 30 minutes ends up at the more scenic Na Mueang 2 Waterfall.

do.what: Chaweng nightlife: ARKbar beach fire shows, Soi Green Mango

source.quote: ARKbar currently advertises fire shows every evening from 20:00 to midnight, weather permitting.

sleep.area: Chaweng (busiest, most hotels, nightlife) or Bophut / Fisherman's Village (boutique, calmer); Lamai = mid-range value

source.quote: Chaweng: busiest, most hotels, nightlife access

more_sources.quote: Bophut: Fisherman’s Village charm, boutique hotels
Lamai: quieter beach, good restaurants, mid-range value

next.how: Fly from Samui Airport (USM) with Bangkok Airways (near-hourly to BKK, codeshare Thai Airways), ~1h15. Samui is placed last for exactly this reason. Note: Samui flights are comparatively expensive (3,000-5,000 THB per Wikivoyage); cheaper alternative is ferry to Surat Thani + flight/bus.

source.quote: Koh Samui is last on this two-week Thailand island-hopping itinerary because it has a small airport from which you can fly back to Bangkok or Phuket.

more_sources.quote: They have near-hourly departures to/from Bangkok (BKK), codesharing with Thai Airways for easy connections.
Traveling by plane is the fastest way to get from Koh Samui to Bangkok.
Fastest Transport 1h 15m
